summary: A focused Ekkamai stop for pad kaprao (Thai holy-basil stir-fry) at Phed Mark, a small restaurant directly opposite Ekkamai Bus Terminal and a short walk from BTS Ekkamai. The menu centers on the dish, with pork and beef shown on the official site and spice choices from normal through the house Phed Mark level.
whyGo: Try a Bangkok restaurant built around one familiar Thai comfort dish, served with a choice of protein and heat.
Easy to combine with an Ekkamai transit stop: the venue says it is one minute on foot from BTS Ekkamai.
bestFor: Pad kaprao fans who want to compare a focused specialist with everyday Thai versions.
Travelers comfortable with casual dining and some uncertainty about queues.
skipIf: You need a broad menu, a quiet sit-down meal, or guaranteed short waits.
You avoid chilli entirely: even the restaurant's normal setting may taste hot to some diners; ask staff for the mildest option and confirm before ordering.
duration: Allow about 45–90 minutes for a meal, including a possible queue; this is a planning estimate. Recent customer reports describe waits ranging from around 15 minutes to much longer, so timing is unpredictable.
cost: Official site lists pork at ฿105 and beef at ฿155. Budget roughly ฿110–฿200 per person for a main and possible add-ons; the upper figure is a planning estimate, and current December prices may change.
hours: Official site currently lists Monday–Saturday, 11:00–17:00, and Sunday closed. Recheck before travelling, especially around holidays or year-end.
bestTime: Go near opening on a weekday to improve your chances of a shorter wait. A Wongnai diner reported arriving at 15:00 without a queue in August 2025, but this is one visit and not a reliable guarantee.
gettingThere: Take BTS Sukhumvit Line to Ekkamai. The restaurant's directions say use Exit 3, turn around at street level, pass the 7-Eleven, and cross toward the Ekkamai Bus Terminal. The official site describes the walk as one minute. Address shown there: 928 Sukhumvit Road; Wongnai lists 300 Sukhumvit Road, so follow the official directions/map pin rather than relying on the differing street numbers.
booking: No booking method is listed on the official site. Expect walk-in service; confirm current policy directly if you need certainty.
accessibility: The official information describes a street-level location across from the bus terminal, but does not publish step-free access, seating, restroom, or wheelchair details. The short approach includes crossing Sukhumvit Road; check the crossing and entrance conditions on arrival.
practicalTips: Choose a lower heat setting if unsure and ask staff to explain the available levels; diners have reported that even milder settings can feel spicy.
The restaurant's concept is pad kaprao, not a broad Thai menu; ask about current protein and dietary options before making a special trip.
Arrive with schedule flexibility, as recent visitor accounts mention queues and order delays.
Check current opening hours and prices on the official website before going.
decemberNotes: December 2026 opening hours, holiday closures, prices, and queue conditions have not been announced in the sources checked. The published weekly schedule is the current baseline only; verify close to the visit. No special December event is identified.
uncertainties: Hours and menu prices can change before December 2026; online sources also show different street numbers for the location.
No official accessibility details, reservation information, or reliable wait-time estimate are published.
